item.title: Comisión Permanente resuelve en vivo si convoca a periodo extraordinario por comisionados del INAI
item.description: The Senate’s Standing Committee decided to reject the call for an extraordinary session to elect the commissioners of the National Institute for Transparency, Access to Information and Personal Data Protection (INAI), determining that these appointments do not constitute a legislative urgency. This resolution prevents the institute from reaching the quorum required to resume its sessions immediately, leaving the decision pending for ordinary processing in the First Committee. This move contrasts with the previously approved request by the Political Coordination Board, highlighting an internal political dispute over the priority of filling these vital vacancies. The debate reflected deep political divisions, with Morena legislators arguing against the alleged interference of the Judicial Branch in legislative matters, while the opposition accused the ruling majority of seeking to conceal irregularities by preventing the INAI from functioning. Senator Kenia López Rabadán strongly criticized the government’s stance, suggesting political disinterest and possible intentions to weaken the institution. The lack of agreement has left the body inoperative since April, raising concerns about the State’s capacity to guarantee transparency and access to public information. This development is relevant to open data because an inoperative INAI directly compromises the supervision and protection of the right to public information. Without the institute’s full functioning, it becomes more difficult to ensure government accountability and guarantee transparency in the management of public resources, which are essential for the integrity of open data. The political paralysis of the regulatory body underscores the vulnerability of transparency structures to partisan dynamics, affecting civil society’s ability to demand clarity in the data issued by the State.

item.title: Costa Rica. Diputados presentan proyecto de ley elaborado por ChatGPT
item.description: Costa Rica has introduced a groundbreaking legislative proposal to regulate artificial intelligence, uniquely drafted entirely by ChatGPT-4. This initiative prioritizes human rights, aiming to ensure transparency, privacy, and data security while fostering the development of explainable AI systems. By mandating a registry for algorithms and security measures, the law seeks to protect citizens in an increasingly automated landscape. This project is highly relevant to the open data community because it establishes a framework for mandatory disclosure of AI functionalities and underlying algorithms. Such transparency requirements directly encourage the publication of structured data regarding system operations, which is essential for auditing, research, and public accountability. It demonstrates how open information policies can coexist with robust ethical regulations. Ultimately, this move highlights the potential of using generative AI as a tool for legislative drafting itself. It signals a proactive national stance on emerging technologies, encouraging other nations to consider similar regulatory models. The proposal underscores the intersection of open governance and technological innovation, setting a precedent for how societies might govern digital futures through inclusive, data-informed policy making.

item.title: Digital Renaissance: Cash-in App is set to Empower Extraordinary Lifestyle Shifts in the Emerging Digital Economy | TechCabal
item.description: The digital economy has fundamentally reshaped human lifestyle by prioritizing hyperconnectivity and data-driven personalization. This shift has rendered traditional physical interactions, such as handwritten letters or cash transactions, largely obsolete, replacing them with seamless, automated digital alternatives. The emergence of instant communication tools and remote work options demonstrates how technology has redefined convenience, allowing individuals to manage their lives and careers with unprecedented flexibility and efficiency. A critical implication of this transformation is the move toward trustless, automated interactions facilitated by blockchain and digital currencies. Businesses and consumers now favor solutions that eliminate the need for manual oversight or institutional trust, relying instead on smart contracts and instant settlement systems. This demand for automation drives the adoption of platforms that bridge traditional and digital finance, ensuring that value exchange is transparent, immediate, and accessible regardless of geographic location. This article is highly relevant to open data because the digital economy’s infrastructure relies entirely on the continuous collection, analysis, and sharing of machine-readable information. Open data principles enable the hyperconnectivity and interoperability required for these new business models to thrive, particularly in cross-border payments and remote collaboration. By fostering transparent, accessible data ecosystems, we support the technological evolution that drives economic innovation and enhances user experience in an increasingly connected world.

item.title: El IPC de Francia se modera al 5,1% en mayo
item.description: French inflation moderated significantly in May, driven by slowing price increases across the energy, food, manufacturing, and services sectors. This deceleration underscores the effectiveness of broader economic stabilization efforts within the Eurozone. The data illustrates how real-time price monitoring can reveal underlying inflationary pressures. Such granular insights enable policymakers to adjust strategies with precision, ensuring that temporary shocks do not become entrenched trends. This information is crucial for open data initiatives, as it provides a transparent and verifiable record of economic health. Access to such high-quality statistical datasets allows researchers and citizens to independently analyze trends and hold institutions accountable for their economic management.

item.title: Freedom of Information statistics: October to December 2022
item.description: This article highlights the release of quarterly statistics on Freedom of Information Act implementation within UK central government bodies, confirming their status as National Statistics. This designation ensures the data meets rigorous standards for trustworthiness and quality, as regulated by the UK Statistics Authority. The ongoing assessment underscores the government’s commitment to transparent, high-quality data production. By maintaining these standards, official statistics effectively support public decision-making and foster informed debate on government accountability. This is highly relevant to open data because it demonstrates the institutional framework required for reliable public sector transparency. It shows how statutory obligations combine with strict statistical governance to ensure that open government data remains accurate, accessible, and valuable for citizen engagement.

item.title: Halliburton - Halliburton Upgrades Norwegian Petroleum Directorate's National Data Repository - Advanced system is industry's first fully cloud-native national data repository implementation
item.description: Cookie consent mechanisms empower users to control personal data collection, aligning with open data principles of transparency and informed consent. This ensures ethical handling of user information during browsing analytics.

item.title: Halliburton Launches Diskos 2.0 NDR for Norwegian Petroleum Directorate
item.description: Halliburton’s Diskos 2.0 represents a significant leap in data infrastructure by being the industry’s first fully cloud-native National Data Repository. This architecture allows users to access and analyze extensive exploration and production data directly within functional software environments, eliminating the need to move information to local networks. By integrating automation and artificial intelligence, the system enhances scalability while significantly reducing storage costs and processing inefficiencies. This approach fundamentally improves how stakeholders interact with complex datasets. Operators, service companies, and academic institutions gain immediate, transparent access to critical seismic and well data without cumbersome copying procedures. The platform’s ability to connect with third-party services further enriches its utility, enabling faster, more informed decision-making through streamlined analytics and interpretation workflows. This development is highly relevant to open_data principles as it demonstrates the power of cloud-native systems in making vast, specialized datasets more accessible and usable. By removing physical data barriers and fostering a transparent, collaborative environment, such platforms encourage broader participation and innovation. Ultimately, it shows how modern infrastructure can transform static data into actionable insights, supporting sustainable industry growth and global energy security.

item.title: Halliburton upgrades NDR for Norwegian Petroleum Directorate
item.description: Halliburton’s new Diskos 2.0 transforms Norway’s national data repository by leveraging cloud-native technology and artificial intelligence. This upgrade enables seamless access to vast petroleum data without the need for local data movement, significantly reducing costs and enhancing scalability for the industry. By allowing direct interaction with petrotechnical software, the system accelerates the journey from raw data to actionable insights. This immediate availability supports better decision-making for operators and stakeholders, fostering a transparent environment that streamlines complex data processing and interpretation tasks across diverse professional groups. This evolution is crucial for open data as it demonstrates how modern cloud infrastructure can make massive, specialized datasets more accessible and interoperable. By removing traditional barriers to data usage, it encourages broader collaboration and innovation, proving that open access to high-quality, managed data drives investment and efficiency in critical sectors like energy.

item.title: How is this humane or ethical, asks the Animal Protection Party of Canada
item.description: Animal welfare groups condemn Ontario’s planned expansion of sporting dog compounds, arguing that training methods involving live wild animals constitute inherent cruelty. The release of an internal association letter highlights the intense stress placed on coyotes, foxes, and hares exposed to numerous dogs and participants. Critics assert that such practices violate fundamental animal welfare standards, as the environment is designed for dog training rather than the safety of the wildlife victims used as bait. The article argues that humane alternatives, such as scent-based training, are readily available and would eliminate the need to chase or kill wild animals. Experts question the feasibility of claims that organizers maintain complete control over hounds, suggesting that the current system relies on exploiting wildlife for sport. There is a strong call to ban the use of live animals in both compounds and general landscapes, emphasizing that pitting multiple dogs against a single wild victim is barbaric and inhumane. This issue is critically relevant to open data because the exposure of the Ontario Sporting Dog Association’s internal letter demonstrates the power of Freedom of Information requests in revealing hidden institutional realities. It underscores how transparent access to government and organizational records allows activists to challenge opaque legislation, like Bill 91, and mobilize public outrage against policies that prioritize industrial interests over ecological and ethical concerns.

item.title: How many years will you need to work to afford a Jerusalem apartment?
item.description: This data highlights the severe housing affordability crisis in Israel, revealing that purchasing a home requires an unrealistic number of years’ income for the average citizen. The disparity between regions is stark, with some areas demanding nearly three decades of work, illustrating a systemic failure in making housing accessible to the general population. The relevance to open data lies in the transparency of these socioeconomic metrics. By making granular statistics on income-to-price ratios and construction timelines publicly available, citizens and policymakers can critically analyze market disparities. This openness is essential for driving accountability and fostering informed discussions on necessary legislative reforms to address the housing shortage.

item.title: Israeli Health Ministry takes aim at Elon Musk's COVID claims
item.description: Elon Musk’s tweet, citing an Israeli Health Ministry letter that reported no known COVID deaths among healthy individuals under fifty, ignited a significant dispute over data transparency. While Musk used the statement to argue the virus poses minimal risk to young, healthy populations, the Health Ministry immediately labeled his comment as “fake news.” This contradiction highlights the chaotic nature of information dissemination during public health crises, where official stances can shift rapidly or inconsistently, causing public confusion and undermining trust in authoritative sources. The controversy underscores the critical challenges in open_data initiatives, particularly regarding data completeness and clinical verification. The ministry admitted its database was incomplete and relied on self-reported information rather than comprehensive clinical records. This gap between limited epidemiological data and detailed medical records demonstrates that open datasets are often preliminary and subject to revision. Without clear protocols for updating public information as new evidence emerges, open data can be easily misinterpreted, leading to the spread of misinformation by influential figures who lack context. This incident is highly relevant to open_data because it illustrates the fragility of public data ecosystems when standards for accuracy and update mechanisms are weak. It emphasizes the necessity for robust metadata and clear disclaimers about data limitations to prevent misrepresentation. Furthermore, it shows how open data must be coupled with education on its provisional nature to ensure it informs rather than polarizes public discourse. Ensuring data integrity and transparency is essential for maintaining credibility and facilitating informed decision-making in a digital age.

item.title: La economía de India registra un sólido crecimiento anual de 7,2%
item.description: India’s economic resilience stands out as a global anomaly, defying severe international headwinds such as geopolitical conflicts and tightening financial conditions. While major economies face stagnation or recession driven by energy crises and inflation, India has achieved robust growth fueled by strong domestic consumption and a thriving services sector. This performance not only surpasses regional competitors but also highlights the nation’s ability to withstand external shocks, maintaining momentum despite importing the vast majority of its energy needs. The consistency of this expansion, which exceeded market expectations, underscores significant internal strengths and effective policy responses. Government spending and consumer activity have been pivotal in sustaining this trajectory, allowing the country to reduce its current account deficit and cool inflationary pressures. These improvements position India favorably against other large economies that are struggling with persistent price hikes and reduced growth rates, marking a distinct divergence in global economic health. This narrative is vital to open data advocacy as it demonstrates how transparent, publicly available statistics can reveal deeper structural realities beyond superficial trends. Reliable data infrastructure enables policymakers and analysts to accurately assess resilience and predict future stability, fostering evidence-based decision-making. By making economic indicators accessible, societies can better understand how specific sectors drive national success, encouraging accountability and informed public discourse on economic governance.

item.title: La inflación en Italia se desacelera en mayo al 7,6%
item.description: Italian inflation decelerated in May, primarily driven by falling energy costs. This easing of pressure offers relief to household budgets and suggests a stabilizing economic environment, despite previous highs. Gross domestic product growth was revised upward for the first quarter, indicating stronger economic expansion than initially estimated. This positive adjustment reflects resilience in consumer spending and business activity during the early months of the year. This data is relevant to open data initiatives, as it underscores the importance of accessible, real-time economic statistics for public analysis. Transparent reporting enables citizens and researchers to monitor inflation trends and assess policy effectiveness across European nations.

item.title: La producción chilena de cobre cae en medio de un potencial impulso al mercado
item.description: Chile’s declining copper production underscores persistent supply instabilities, driven by project delays, water restrictions, and lower ore quality. These structural challenges disrupt global markets that are already grappling with weak Chinese demand, creating price volatility despite the modest year-over-year decline. This situation is critical for open data because transparent, accessible mining statistics enable analysts to accurately track these supply shocks. Without reliable public data, stakeholders cannot properly assess the impact of environmental constraints on commodity flows, hindering informed decision-making in an increasingly volatile sector.

item.title: Las mujeres víctimas de violencia de género aumentaron un 8,3% en 2022, hasta 32.644
item.description: Datos abiertos

item.title: Las víctimas de violencia de género suben un 8% en 2022, con casi 33.000 mujeres maltratadas
item.description: The 2022 statistical report reveals a significant escalation in gender-based violence in Spain, marking a clear trend toward increased prevalence and legal intervention. The rise in the number of victims and protective measures underscores the urgency of addressing this systemic issue, highlighting that violence against partners remains a critical social challenge requiring sustained attention and resources. This data serves as a vital public indicator of the current state of gender equality and safety, driving policy debates on victim support and prevention strategies. A parallel analysis of domestic violence shows a contrasting trajectory, with a slight decline in the number of victims but a sharp increase in the issuance of protective orders. This divergence suggests evolving reporting behaviors or shifts in how authorities categorize and respond to family conflicts. The high volume of measures against male perpetrators in both categories indicates a persistent gendered pattern in interpersonal violence, reinforcing the need for specialized judicial protocols that recognize the distinct nature of these crimes. These findings are profoundly relevant to open data initiatives because they demonstrate the essential role of transparent, accessible government statistics in ensuring accountability and raising public awareness. By making such granular data available, policymakers and researchers can identify regional hotspots, evaluate the effectiveness of current legal frameworks, and allocate resources more efficiently. Open data transforms these raw numbers into actionable insights, empowering civil society to monitor progress and demand stricter enforcement of rights, ensuring that statistical transparency directly contributes to tangible social improvements and justice.

item.title: Mayoría de campesinos de Veracruz, afectados por altos costos de insumos
item.description: High input costs and climate-related factors severely affect most agricultural producers in Veracruz, highlighting systemic vulnerabilities within rural economies. These challenges underscore the urgent need for transparent and accessible data to inform effective policy interventions. Public statistical agencies such as INEGI provide crucial evidence of these hardships; however, the raw nature of census data often requires further standardization. This dataset is vital for open data initiatives because it reveals the specific socio-economic barriers faced by farmers. By making this information openly available, researchers and policymakers can better design targeted solutions to stabilize the agricultural sector and support affected communities.

item.title: New Global Trade Data Portal offers real-time access to trade data
item.description: Global disruptions have highlighted the critical need for timely, detailed data to safeguard food security and manage complex supply chains. The launch of the Global Trade Data Portal addresses this by providing real-time insights into trade flows, enabling policymakers to make informed decisions and respond swiftly to emerging risks. This access to granular data transforms how nations understand and mitigate potential shocks to global value chains. Central to this effort are interactive dashboards tracking maritime grain trade, such as those for wheat and oilseeds. These tools offer frequent updates on shipment trends across numerous economies, shifting logistics strategies from efficiency to resilience. By visualizing where and how goods move, stakeholders can assess short-term trade dynamics and infrastructure demands in a rapidly changing environment. This initiative is vital for open data as it exemplifies the public sector’s role in democratizing access to high-value economic information. By aggregating and visualizing complex trade statistics, the WTO enhances transparency and supports international cooperation. Such accessible, real-time datasets empower diverse actors to collaborate effectively, ensuring that global trade mechanisms remain robust and responsive during crises.

item.title: News about open_data on 2023-06-01
Privacy Policy
item.description: This article details the standard privacy practices of a Greek website, highlighting how user interaction translates into data collection. It specifically warns users against uploading images containing embedded location data, as this information remains accessible to other visitors. This serves as a critical reminder for anyone handling public datasets: metadata can inadvertently expose sensitive personal information, emphasizing the need for rigorous data sanitization in open data initiatives. The site also outlines its use of cookies and third-party services, such as Gravatar and automated spam detection, which monitor user activity and store identifiers like IP addresses. While these tools enhance security and convenience, they create complex data trails that extend beyond the primary website. Understanding these layers is essential for open data advocates who must assess how seemingly anonymous actions can be linked to specific individuals through cross-site tracking and persistent identifiers. Ultimately, the policy grants users rights to access, edit, or delete their personal information, reflecting a commitment to transparency and user control. This is relevant to open data because it illustrates the balance between maintaining functional, secure web platforms and respecting individual privacy. As open data promotes the release of information, it must also consider the ethical implications of metadata and user-generated content, ensuring that openness does not compromise the confidentiality of those who interact with the platform.

item.title: REDACTED: Your right to know | A Crikey series
item.description: Transparency empowers citizens.

item.title: Reddit Joins Twitter In Squeezing Devs With Unreasonable Fees - SlashGear
item.description: Apollo’s developer faces unsustainable costs due to Reddit’s new API pricing, which drastically exceeds both subscription fees and actual user revenue. This economic mismatch threatens the app’s viability, forcing a choice between raising prices significantly or shutting down the service. The situation highlights the fragility of third-party apps that rely on open data access from major platforms. Without fair licensing terms, independent developers cannot maintain their services, potentially limiting user choice and data portability in the broader ecosystem. This conflict underscores the importance of open data principles, as restrictive policies may drive users to alternative platforms. The potential exodus to open-source social networks illustrates how centralized control over data access can disrupt established communities and hinder innovation.

item.title: Se incrementó 6.2% superficie de uso agrícola en Michoacán
item.description: Recent preliminary data from Mexico’s 2022 Agricultural Census reveal that agricultural land use in Michoacán has expanded over the past fifteen years, securing the state a prominent position among Mexico’s leading producers. This growth underscores the region’s enduring importance to the national food supply chain and highlights the sector’s resilience despite broader economic shifts. At the same time, the census indicates a fragmentation of landholdings, with the average size of active production units shrinking even as their total number increases. This trend suggests a shift toward smaller-scale farming operations, challenging traditional models of large agricultural enterprises and pointing to evolving land management strategies across the state. The report also sheds light on demographic changes, noting a predominantly male workforce and rising levels of primary education among farmers. These findings are crucial for open data initiatives, as they provide transparent, granular insights into rural demographics and land distribution, enabling policymakers and researchers to better address issues of equity, education, and sustainable agricultural development.

item.title: Zepeda: Armenta y Monreal pagarían de su bolsa multas
item.description: The Mexican Senate imposes personal fines on legislators who fail to appoint commissioners to the National Institute for Transparency, Access to Information and Personal Data Protection (INAI), underscoring the legal consequences of obstructing transparency institutions. This situation highlights the critical link between judicial enforcement and the functioning of open data governance bodies. Ultimately, it emphasizes that accountability mechanisms are essential to ensure public access to information and protect citizens’ data rights.

The article illustrates how online platforms routinely collect personal and browsing data via cookies for tracking and advertising. This highlights critical open data concerns regarding privacy and consent mechanisms. It underscores the necessity for transparent data practices to protect user rights while enabling responsible data usage.

The surge in imported vehicles, particularly from Asia, is fundamentally reshaping Mexico’s automotive market and logistics landscape. This shift highlights a critical mismatch between supply and infrastructure, as current transport capacity struggles to accommodate the influx of goods from new origins. To address these operational gaps, major logistics firms are establishing specialized divisions and partnerships designed to streamline the movement of imported cars. By integrating specialized fleets with existing terminal networks, these companies aim to improve supply chain efficiency and support both import distribution and future export capabilities. This trend is vital for open data enthusiasts because it underscores the growing need for transparent, standardized information in complex, cross-border supply chains. As logistics networks evolve to handle diverse international flows, the demand for accessible, real-time data on trade volumes, infrastructure utilization, and operational metrics becomes essential for analyzing market dynamics and informing policy decisions.

The implementation of the Transactional User Amount regulation requires individuals to set transfer limits, with the aim of preventing fraud and identity theft. This regulatory shift prioritizes security by mandating user authorization for transactions that exceed the established threshold, thereby strengthening protection against electronic fraud. This initiative is relevant to open data as it illustrates how regulatory frameworks can leverage financial technology data to protect users. By requiring active user participation in configuring security settings, it underscores the critical role of transparent data practices and user control in modern digital finance systems. Users have until early 2026 to define their limits; after this deadline, banks will apply default values. This transition highlights the evolving responsibility in data management, ensuring that personal financial information is handled with stricter oversight and that individuals retain control over their transactional boundaries within the digital economy.

The provisional data released by the National Statistics Institute (INE) indicates that inflation in Spain has significantly moderated to 3.2%, marking its lowest level since July 2021. This decline is primarily driven by reduced fuel prices and a stabilization in the cost of the household shopping basket. Notably, the annual price variation fell below previous levels, including the comparative low of March 2022, suggesting that the initial shock from the energy crisis linked to the war in Ukraine has passed. Consequently, prices actually experienced a slight monthly decrease compared to April, providing a temporary respite for consumers’ purchasing power. Beyond the general index, underlying inflation also decreased for the third consecutive month, reaching 6.1%. This metric, which excludes volatile energy and unprocessed food prices, is crucial for understanding the true trajectory of price stability in the economy. The downward trend in underlying inflation reinforces the government’s narrative that current policies are effective and aligns with the European Commission’s revised forecasts, which anticipate an average inflation rate of 4% for 2023 and a further decline to 2.7% in 2024. However, projections also warn that underlying price pressures may remain more persistent than headline figures suggest. This article is highly relevant to open data enthusiasts and analysts because it highlights the importance of distinguishing between headline inflation and underlying metrics when assessing economic health. The provisional nature of the data underscores the need for continuous monitoring as final figures are released, illustrating how real-time statistical updates influence public policy and international economic forecasts. Understanding the divergence between energy-driven volatility and core price trends is essential for interpreting the efficacy of governmental measures and anticipating future economic stability in the European Union context.

The Fifth National Action Plan for Open Government 2022–2024 highlights transparency, accountability, and citizen participation as essential tools for innovating public management. By engaging various government ministries and civil society organizations, the plan aims to build an open, federal state that delivers effective policies and promotes social inclusion. This collaborative approach seeks to restore public trust by ensuring that government actions are responsive to societal needs and demands. A central focus is the Ministry of Public Works’ commitment to institutionalizing citizen oversight in public infrastructure projects. Through the creation of an Observatory and a manual of standards, the ministry fosters a model where accountability serves as a driving force for improvement. This strategy integrates local and provincial actors, reorienting priorities based on civil society feedback and establishing a cooperative framework for managing public resources and infrastructure. This initiative is highly relevant to open data because it operationalizes transparency through digital tools such as MapaInversiones. By providing real-time visibility into public investments and enabling citizens to report irregularities, the platform transforms raw data into actionable public oversight. Furthermore, the creation of a repository of experiences and shared information platforms demonstrates how open data facilitates collective policy improvement, ensuring that civic engagement is grounded in accessible, reliable, and timely information.

High homicide rates in South Africa contrast with official claims of improvement, revealing a complex security landscape. While some violent crimes decreased, others escalated, highlighting the limitations of isolated statistics. This case underscores the critical need for comprehensive open data to verify governmental narratives. Transparent access to diverse crime metrics allows for accurate assessment of public safety and fosters necessary accountability.
Leaders demand clarity regarding external interference. The public expects answers about this lack of transparency. This underscores the urgent need for open data on foreign influence.

This article highlights a contentious debate regarding government transparency and the practical challenges of fulfilling public-records requests. Mayoral challenger Tom Goldenberg argues that the Elicker administration is failing to provide timely access to information, citing a nearly three-month delay in responding to a specific inquiry about methadone clinics. He compares New Haven’s high volume of unresolved complaints unfavorably to Bridgeport, asserting that the current level of opacity undermines public trust and hinders accountability. In defense, Mayor Justin Elicker emphasizes the massive scale of the city’s workload, noting that it processes approximately ten thousand Freedom of Information Act requests annually. He contends that the delay is not due to negligence but rather a necessary legal review process to protect confidential data and privileged information. The mayor points to recent infrastructure improvements, such as new digital portals and dedicated staff, as evidence of systemic efforts to balance thoroughness with efficiency. This conflict is relevant to open data because it exposes the friction between the public’s demand for immediate transparency and the administrative realities of data management, privacy, and legal compliance. It raises critical questions about whether current statutory timeframes are realistic for modern municipalities and whether improved technological tools can bridge the gap between rapid public access and responsible information handling. The dispute illustrates the ongoing struggle to define what constitutes reasonable responsiveness in an era of high information demand.

The Supreme Court annulled a fiscal reform that had allowed the tax agency to share private identity verification data with businesses. This decision prioritizes individual privacy rights, ruling that the mechanism insufficiently protected sensitive biometric information from unauthorized third-party access. The ruling highlights that enabling such services without strict consent safeguards constitutes a violation of data protection principles. Consequently, the government can no longer use this specific legal basis to leverage public data for private commercial purposes, reinforcing the boundary between state authority and personal rights. This case is vital for open data governance, as it establishes that transparency and data utility must never compromise fundamental privacy rights. It serves as a critical precedent, demonstrating that even beneficial digital services require rigorous legal constraints to prevent the misuse of sensitive citizen information.

Air New Zealand collects anonymous passenger weight data to optimize flight loads. This initiative highlights the practical challenges of gathering sensitive personal information for operational efficiency. It is relevant to open data as it demonstrates how anonymization enables the sharing of utility data while respecting privacy standards.

item.title: AEMEND urges PM Shehbaz to take notice of enforced disappearances of journalists
item.description: AEMEND condemns the enforced disappearances of journalists, urging immediate state intervention to ensure their safe recovery and legal due process. This stance underscores the critical importance of protecting press freedom, a fundamental pillar of open data ecosystems where information must remain accessible and secure from arbitrary suppression. The association warns against the politicization of media workers and highlights undeclared censorship by state institutions. Such practices restrict the flow of unbiased information, directly compromising the transparency and impartiality required for healthy democratic discourse and the reliable dissemination of public knowledge. These revelations are vital to the open_data community as they illustrate how political pressure and censorship threaten the integrity of information sources. By restricting access to accurate data and promoting one-sided narratives, authorities undermine the very foundations of open information systems essential for accountability and informed citizenship.

item.title: Baja tasa de desempleo en México 2.7% en primer trimestre del 2023: Inegi
item.description: Mexico’s labor market showed significant recovery in early 2023, with unemployment falling to historic lows and active workforce participation rising substantially. This improvement reflects a robust reintegration of workers into the formal economy, particularly in the commerce and manufacturing sectors. However, a substantial portion of the labor force remains underemployed, highlighting challenges in job quality and hours availability despite the overall decline in unemployment. Crucially, this positive employment trend coexists with a rise in labor informality and persistent gender disparities. Over half of the workforce is engaged in informal activities, lacking social protections, while female labor participation remains significantly lower than that of men. These structural issues undermine the sustainability of job growth and indicate that economic recovery has not been evenly distributed across demographic groups or sectors. This data is vital for the open_data community as it underscores the necessity of accessible, granular statistical information to monitor socio-economic conditions. Transparent labor metrics enable researchers, policymakers, and civil society to identify inefficiencies, advocate for equitable reforms, and hold institutions accountable. Open access to such detailed indicators fosters evidence-based decision-making and promotes transparency in public administration.

item.title: Buscan transparentar el registro de licencias de importaciones para agilizar las solicitudes y evitar discrecionalidades
item.description: Deputies from the Civic Coalition propose the creation of an Open Import Data Portal in Argentina, aiming to replace the current discretionary nature of the SIRA system with a transparent and predictable management framework. The project requires that all information regarding import applications, including product details and status, be published digitally in open formats. This measure seeks to eliminate abuses of power and significantly reduce corruption risks associated with the granting of licenses. The initiative establishes strict and automatic deadlines for resolving applications, granting approval if no response is issued within the specified timeframe. Additionally, it proposes simplifying administrative procedures and making public the criteria for economic capacity, thereby ensuring traceability and predictability in commercial operations. This addresses the criticism that recurrent modifications to the current system primarily serve to restrict imports and unjustifiably protect the Central Bank’s reserves. This article is relevant to open data because it illustrates how the systematic publication of public information in accessible formats is a fundamental tool against corruption and state arbitrariness. It demonstrates that transparency is not merely a technical requirement, but a governance mechanism that empowers citizens and businesses, enabling them to monitor compliance with regulations and reduce the information asymmetry that favors bureaucratic discretion.

item.title: Construyendo redes para la transparencia
item.description: Effective transparency in Mexico depends fundamentally on the coordinated interaction among three key actors: citizens who request information, institutions obligated to respond, and guaranteeing bodies that resolve conflicts. This system operates as an integrated network in which requests activate the right to information, responses generate accountability, and resolutions ensure justice. The strength of this democratic structure lies in the ability of these groups to collaborate, ensuring that access to public information is not merely a theoretical right but a robust, everyday practice. The recent creation of the Federal Network of Transparency Units represents a crucial advance by centralizing the knowledge and best practices of officials responsible for managing requests from citizens. These units serve as the first point of contact with the public and are essential allies in expediting the processing of thousands of weekly requests. By fostering the exchange of experiences across different levels of government, the initiative aims to improve the quality and timeliness of responses, thereby reducing the volume of disputes that reach higher review bodies. This initiative is particularly relevant to the open data movement, as it demonstrates that transparency is not an isolated process but a network of institutional collaboration. When transparency units share resources and optimize their protocols, they not only benefit immediate citizens but also strengthen the infrastructure necessary for a more open government. Given the recent paralysis of the guaranteeing body, these parallel networks help maintain democratic activity and data protection, ensuring that civil society continues to have access to public information even during periods of institutional instability.

item.title: Desempleo se ubicó en 8,8% en abril, ligeramente por encima del 8,6% registrado en marzo
item.description: The latest labor data from the National Institute of Statistics and Geography (INE) reveals a slight increase in unemployment, marking the second consecutive monthly rise. This trend underscores ongoing volatility in the job market, contrasting with previous periods of decline. Analyzing these shifts is crucial for understanding the broader economic health and labor dynamics within the country. Disaggregated analysis shows higher unemployment rates in the interior regions compared to the capital, highlighting regional disparities. Employment and activity rates also vary by location, indicating that economic participation is not uniform across the nation. Such granular insights help identify specific areas requiring targeted policy interventions to address uneven labor market performance. Furthermore, significant portions of the workforce face underemployment and lack social security registration. These metrics expose underlying structural vulnerabilities, such as informal labor practices and the underutilization of skills. For open data initiatives, this article demonstrates how detailed, granular datasets are essential for diagnosing economic inequalities. Transparent access to such statistics empowers researchers and citizens to hold institutions accountable and drive informed public discourse on labor rights and economic policy.

item.title: Estudiantes apoyan al pleno del INAI
item.description: The article highlights the crucial role of the INAI in protecting democratic institutions through transparency. Public support from university students underscores that access to information is essential for addressing societal challenges and holding public authorities accountable. This illustrates how citizen engagement strengthens open data initiatives by reinforcing institutional trust and the collective defense of civic rights against potential vulnerabilities.

item.title: Group Slams Buhari’s Administration Over FOI Violations | African Examiner
item.description: The Media Rights Agenda’s report on the Buhari administration exposes a systemic failure in implementing Nigeria’s Freedom of Information Act, establishing a troubling legacy of institutional secrecy. Public agencies routinely withheld information and ignored reporting obligations without consequence, effectively normalizing a culture of opacity. This widespread non-compliance undermined the Act’s core purpose of ensuring government transparency and accountability to the citizenry. Despite the law requiring annual reporting by all federal institutions, compliance remained exceptionally low, with only a tiny fraction of agencies submitting the necessary documents. The Attorney General’s office failed to enforce penalties or update guidelines to reflect modern technological advancements, leaving oversight mechanisms ineffective. This lack of enforcement signaled official indifference to the legal mandates, allowing impunity to flourish across the civil service and eroding public trust in government operations. This case highlights the critical link between legislative frameworks and open data practices, demonstrating that laws alone are insufficient without active enforcement and resource allocation. For the open_data community, the report serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of unimplemented transparency policies. It underscores the urgent need for the incoming administration to prioritize proactive disclosure, adequate budgeting, and strict adherence to information access laws to truly foster a culture of accountability.

item.title: Halliburton upgrades Norwegian Petroleum national data repository
item.description: The Norwegian Petroleum Directorate has launched Diskos 2.0, the industry’s first fully cloud-native National Data Repository. This upgrade integrates advanced automation and AI to manage massive datasets efficiently, significantly reducing storage costs while enhancing scalability and processing power for exploration and production insights. A key innovation is the ability to access comprehensive seismic and well data directly within third-party software environments without moving or copying data from the repository. This seamless connectivity streamlines analysis, allowing operators and stakeholders to perform complex interpretations instantly within a transparent and clean management environment. This development is highly relevant to open data principles by demonstrating how cloud-native architectures can facilitate secure, frictionless data sharing and access. By removing traditional barriers to data retrieval and enabling immediate analytical use, the system promotes greater transparency and efficiency in the energy sector, setting a precedent for open, accessible data ecosystems.

item.title: Housing crisis deepens as approvals collapse to 13-year low
item.description: The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that dwelling approvals have plummeted to their lowest levels since 2012, driven by significant declines in both houses and units. This sharp contraction in housing supply is particularly alarming as it coincides with record net overseas migration, exacerbating the housing crisis in major population centers like NSW and Victoria. This data highlights a critical disconnect between immigration policy and housing infrastructure, suggesting that current strategies are worsening the affordability crisis and homelessness. The lack of new approvals threatens to deepen inequality and strain urban resources, underscoring the urgent need for policy alignment between population growth and construction capacity. This article is relevant to open data because it demonstrates how accessible government statistics can expose systemic policy failures. By making construction and migration figures publicly available, open data enables analysts to connect disparate datasets, revealing the real-world implications of government decisions on social equity and urban planning.

item.title: Internal Documents Show The FBI Is Only Interested In Punishing Anti-Trump Speech By Its Employees
item.description: The article reveals that the FBI’s enforcement of guidelines against political speech by agents has become inconsistent and vindictive under the Trump administration. While internal rules exist to prevent personal bias from influencing investigations, disciplinary actions were previously rare. However, a sudden flurry of punishments occurred only after agents criticized President Trump, with no similar actions taken against those who criticized or aided other political figures like Hillary Clinton or Mitt Romney. This disparity suggests that the motivation for discipline is not adherence to neutral policy, but rather protection of the President from criticism. This selective enforcement raises serious concerns about the erosion of free speech protections for government employees. The unequal treatment undermines the integrity of the FBI, as it appears to prioritize shielding leadership from dissent over maintaining impartiality. By punishing only negative speech toward the current administration while ignoring equivalent behavior in other contexts, the agency is accused of viewpoint discrimination. This inconsistency weakens public trust and suggests that internal controls are being weaponized to suppress lawful criticism rather than to ensure professional neutrality. This case is critically relevant to open data because the evidence of this discriminatory practice was only uncovered through a Freedom of Information Act request. The necessity of litigation to obtain these documents highlights the essential role of transparency in holding powerful institutions accountable. When governments operate in secrecy, misconduct like politically motivated punishment remains hidden. Open data mechanisms are therefore vital for exposing bias, ensuring that administrative actions are scrutinized for fairness, and preventing the abuse of power through opaque decision-making processes.

item.title: Joan Frawley Desmond - NCRegister
item.description: EWTN reports Catholic news. This illustrates religious media presence. It highlights open data challenges in niche sectors.

item.title: KwaZulu-Natal remains South Africa's murder capital
item.description: South Africa’s fourth-quarter crime statistics reveal a persistent crisis, particularly in KwaZulu-Natal, where murder rates remain the highest nationally. Despite a slight overall decrease in killings, the prevalence of contact crimes and vigilantism highlights systemic vulnerabilities. The data underscores that while certain violent categories, such as child murders, have seen reductions, the broader trend of gender-based violence and attempted assaults against women has surged, indicating a deepening insecurity for vulnerable populations. The government’s response involves significant financial investments aimed at bolstering police capabilities through enhanced visibility and technological integration. Funding is being directed toward tactical teams, community policing forums, and advanced equipment like drones and vehicles. However, the core message remains that crime statistics represent real human lives lost, necessitating a shift from mere quantitative tracking to qualitative protection. The police are doubling efforts to combat contact crimes, emphasizing zero tolerance for violence against children and increased accountability for assaults on women. This report is critically relevant to open data initiatives as it demonstrates how transparent, disaggregated crime statistics can drive policy formulation and resource allocation. By making such granular data public, stakeholders can identify specific hotspots and demographic trends, enabling targeted interventions. Open data serves as a vital tool for holding law enforcement accountable and ensuring that community resources are distributed effectively to address the most pressing safety concerns, thereby fostering trust between citizens and state institutions.

item.title: La inflación se desacelera en España a ocho semanas de las elecciones legislativas
item.description: The article highlights Spain’s significant slowdown in inflation, driven by lower fuel and food prices, bringing the rate closer to the European Central Bank’s target. This trend suggests that recent government interventions, including tax relief on essential goods and broad financial aid packages, have effectively mitigated the erosion of household purchasing power. The stabilization of prices not only improves economic indicators but also serves as a key political argument for the ruling socialist government amid upcoming legislative elections. Despite the positive economic data, the political landscape remains volatile, with the government facing challenges from both right-wing and far-right oppositions. The timing of these inflation figures coincides with a period of electoral uncertainty, as the administration seeks to leverage improved living conditions to counter public discontent and regain political ground. This dynamic illustrates how macroeconomic stability directly influences voter sentiment and political strategies in a competitive democratic environment. This content is relevant to open data because it underscores the critical role of transparent, timely, and accurate statistical releases by national statistical institutes in shaping public perception and policy debate. When official data is accessible and clearly communicated, it allows citizens, analysts, and opposition parties to verify claims about economic health, fostering accountability. Open data acts as a common factual baseline that can either stabilize political narratives or expose discrepancies, thereby ensuring that democratic processes are informed by verifiable evidence rather than speculation.

item.title: Las ventas del comercio minorista se frenan al registrar un crecimiento del 5% en abril
item.description: Retail sales growth slowed significantly in April, signaling a broader economic cooling despite positive monthly fluctuations. This deceleration underscores the vulnerability of consumer spending to changing market conditions, suggesting that prior momentum has largely dissipated. Employment in the sector continued to expand modestly, driven by strong performance in specific regions such as the Balearic Islands and Madrid. However, this uneven geographic distribution highlights persistent disparities in labor demand across different autonomous communities. This data is relevant to open_data initiatives, as it demonstrates how accessible, granular statistical indicators enable real-time monitoring of economic health. By analyzing such open datasets, researchers and policymakers can identify regional imbalances and consumption trends without relying solely on aggregated national figures.

item.title: Los alimentos y las bebidas suben de precio en mayo, pero menos que hace un año - EFEAgro
item.description: May’s projected consumer price index indicates a deceleration in annual inflation to 3.2%, driven primarily by lower fuel prices and a smaller increase in food costs compared to the previous year. This downward trend in both headline and underlying inflation suggests that the worst of the recent price surge may be passing. This data is relevant to open data because it illustrates the value of timely statistical indicators. By providing an early estimate, open data initiatives enable rapid public analysis of economic trends, allowing stakeholders to monitor inflation dynamics before final figures are officially confirmed. Understanding these immediate shifts helps communities and policymakers assess economic pressures more quickly. Access to such provisional statistics fosters transparency and supports informed decision-making regarding cost-of-living impacts, which is a core objective of open government data efforts.

item.title: Los fondos bajistas aumentan su ataque a Cellnex, Enagás y Solaria
item.description: Major institutional investors are increasingly betting against Spanish stocks such as Cellnex, Enagás, and Solaria, signaling a bearish market sentiment. This shift suggests that sophisticated financial actors anticipate significant declines in these specific sectors, potentially reflecting deeper concerns about corporate valuations or sector-specific economic headwinds. The concentrated short interest indicates a loss of confidence among key global players regarding the near-term performance of these companies. Conversely, the paper industry company Ence stands out as the only major stock seeing reduced bearish pressure. This divergence highlights that market skepticism is not uniform across the entire Spanish exchange but is targeted at specific entities facing structural or environmental challenges. The reduction in short positions on Ence may imply that investors view its trajectory as more stable or less risky compared to its peers in the energy and telecommunications sectors. This dynamic is relevant to open data because real-time trading disclosures and institutional positioning metrics are critical components of transparent financial ecosystems. Access to such granular data allows researchers and the public to monitor market sentiment and detect potential anomalies or consensus shifts. By analyzing these open datasets, stakeholders can better understand the invisible forces driving market volatility and assess the health of the economy beyond traditional corporate earnings reports.

item.title: Los precios vuelven a bajar: la inflación cae al 3,2% y la subyacente se frena al 6,1% en mayo
item.description: Spanish inflation has reached its lowest level since mid-2021, driven primarily by falling fuel prices and a moderation in food costs. This significant decline places Spain among the European Union countries with the lowest inflation rates, highlighting a clear downward trend initiated in the first quarter of the year. Although underlying inflation remains elevated, the overall trajectory demonstrates that deflationary pressures are increasingly outweighing inflationary ones, signaling a gradual normalization of price levels across the economy. The persistence of high inflation in the services sector and certain food categories introduces uncertainty, yet experts project a continued progressive slowdown throughout the year. Forecasts suggest a steady convergence toward target levels by 2024, despite potential volatility caused by seasonal effects and environmental factors like drought. The contrast between the rapid initial transmission of energy costs and their slower reversal in production chains underscores the complexity of the current economic adjustment, with analysts expecting further deceleration in the coming months. This article is relevant to open_data because it illustrates how standardized, publicly available statistical indicators, such as the Consumer Price Index (CPI), serve as critical public goods for economic transparency. Reliable open data allows diverse stakeholders, from financial institutions to citizens, to monitor real-time economic health, verify policy effectiveness, and make informed decisions. By democratizing access to official metrics, open data fosters accountability and enables a deeper understanding of macroeconomic trends, ensuring that societal responses to inflation are grounded in verified, accessible evidence rather than speculation.

item.title: New documents show Eby ignored serious warnings about Abbotsford homeless camp: BC United - Indo-Canadian Voice
item.description: The article highlights a critical governance failure where the BC United party alleges Premier David Eby ignored serious health and safety warnings regarding a homeless encampment while serving as Housing Minister. By burying briefing notes that detailed risks such as violence and explosions, the government failed to protect vulnerable individuals and the surrounding community, sparking accusations of political agenda-driven inaction. This incident underscores the vital role of Freedom of Information in holding public officials accountable. It demonstrates how FOI requests can uncover suppressed information and reveal gaps in governmental transparency, allowing opposition parties and citizens to scrutinize decisions that might otherwise remain hidden. The case illustrates the tension between administrative secrecy and public right-to-know. For the open data movement, this story emphasizes the necessity of proactive transparency and accessible government records. It serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of withholding critical safety data, reinforcing the argument that robust open data frameworks are essential for ensuring accountability, preventing harm, and maintaining public trust in democratic institutions.

item.title: News about open_data on 2023-05-31
Opinion: CT shouldn't limit FOIA at its universities
item.description: Senate Bill 1153 proposes significant restrictions on public universities’ transparency obligations, limiting disclosed information strictly to budgetary matters. This shift would effectively shield academic activities from public scrutiny, preventing citizens from identifying issues such as improper animal experimentation or controversial research findings. Consequently, the bill prioritizes institutional privacy over the fundamental democratic principle that public institutions remain accountable to the taxpayers who fund them. Proponents argue that frequent Freedom of Information Act requests harass faculty and hinder research, yet they provide no empirical data to support this claim. The legislation relies on anecdotes rather than evidence, risking the removal of oversight mechanisms for a negligible number of problematic cases. Applying this logic broadly suggests that beneficial public systems should be dismantled due to minority abuse, a flawed reasoning that undermines the integrity of open governance and data accessibility. Current laws already offer various protections for researchers, rendering this sweeping overreach unnecessary. By eliminating broad transparency rights, the bill severely curtails the public’s ability to monitor educational content and societal studies conducted by public universities. This lack of access prevents necessary corrective actions and violates core values of accountability, demonstrating why preserving open data rights is essential for maintaining trust in public education.

item.title: Political Persecution: How the US Govt. Is Silencing the 'Domestic Terrorists' of the Opposition - LewRockwell
item.description: The article argues that the Targeted Violence and Terrorism Prevention (TVTP) grant program, funded by the Department of Homeland Security, is being used to suppress political dissent under the guise of preventing extremism. It claims that taxpayer money is disproportionately supporting institutions and initiatives that label conservative, Christian, and Republican viewpoints as precursors to domestic terrorism. This creates a climate where citizens who hold mainstream political views are systematically monitored and stigmatized by government-funded entities, effectively targeting them as potential threats to national security. Key examples highlight a pattern of conflation between legitimate political expression and violent extremism. The text cites specific university programs and research presentations that equate support for the Second Amendment or adherence to traditional religious beliefs with neo-Nazi ideology. Furthermore, it details instances where funded scholars have advocated for illegal surveillance, infiltration of opposing online communities, and the coordinated de-platforming of conservative voices through pressure on financial and social media services. These actions suggest a coordinated effort to marginalize political opposition rather than genuinely address public safety concerns. This content is relevant to open_data because it underscores the critical importance of transparency in how public funds are allocated and utilized. The article relies on Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) documents to expose the specific activities and ideologies promoted by grant recipients, illustrating how open access to government records can reveal potential abuses of power. It serves as a case study for why open data is essential for holding institutions accountable, allowing the public to scrutinize whether programs intended for broad safety are instead being weaponized for ideological policing.

item.title: Proposed changes to Freedom of Information Act blacked out in documents released to journalists
item.description: The Australian government’s secrecy surrounding proposed amendments to the Freedom of Information Act highlights a critical tension between transparent governance and bureaucratic caution. Although former Information Commissioner Leo Hardiman suggested minor technical fixes to improve the system, these proposals were heavily redacted to protect ongoing government deliberations. This withholding of information, despite the FOI Act’s purpose of enabling public access to records, undermines the very principles the legislation is meant to uphold, suggesting that officials prioritize internal process over public scrutiny. The controversy is further compounded by resource constraints and conflicting narratives regarding the agency’s leadership. The former commissioner resigned citing insufficient funding for processing requests, a claim partially acknowledged by his successor, Angelene Falk, though she denied prior knowledge of the proposed amendments. This disconnect between staff concerns and managerial awareness indicates systemic inefficiencies within the oversight body. When an agency responsible for transparency cannot even agree on the status of its own reform proposals, public trust in its ability to manage open data initiatives is significantly eroded. This case is highly relevant to the open data community because it demonstrates that technical improvements to access laws can be stifled by opaque administrative processes. It serves as a warning that without robust protections against unnecessary secrecy, even minor legislative tweaks aimed at enhancing public access may never see the light of day. For open data advocates, this underscores the necessity of not just legislative reform, but also strict accountability mechanisms to ensure that transparency initiatives are not sacrificed for the sake of bureaucratic convenience or internal political deliberations.

item.title: Querétaro líder en ocupación laboral
item.description: Querétaro leads the nation in labor stability, demonstrating the highest formal employment rates and the lowest underemployment. This performance indicates a robust local economy where job creation has outpaced the previous year, significantly reducing unemployment. The shift toward formal, stable work suggests a healthier labor market structure that benefits workers through better protections and consistent income, contrasting with typical regional volatility. The data reveals a substantial expansion in the economically active population, driven largely by growth in the tertiary sector. Small businesses and service-oriented industries, such as hospitality and diverse services, are primary drivers of this increase. This trend highlights how localized economic growth often relies on the agility of small enterprises to absorb workforce growth, creating opportunities without requiring massive industrial investment. This article is relevant to open data because it showcases the power of public statistical agencies like INEGI in providing transparent, granular labor metrics. By making high-quality, standardized data freely available, researchers and policymakers can identify successful regional models. Open data enables the replication of these positive economic conditions elsewhere, fostering evidence-based decision-making and greater accountability in public administration.

item.title: REDACTED: Your right to know | A Crikey series
item.description: Redacted: Your right to know The article discusses the importance of transparency and access to information in a democratic society. It highlights the challenges faced by individuals and organizations in obtaining public records and emphasizes the need for stronger laws and policies to ensure that information is made available to the public. The author argues that without access to information, citizens are unable to hold their government accountable and make informed decisions.

item.title: Sector logístico de China expande en el primer cuatrimestre
item.description: China’s logistics sector shows stable growth in the early months of the year. Both industrial logistics and total revenues exhibit positive trends, reflecting resilient economic activity. This data underscores the dynamic performance of China’s supply chain. The consistent increase in key metrics indicates sustained demand and operational efficiency within the industry. Such detailed statistical reporting is crucial for open data initiatives. It provides transparent insights into economic trends, enabling researchers and policymakers to access and analyze real-time logistical performance to support better decision-making.

item.title: Senado tiene 3 días para nombrar a comisionado
item.description: A federal judge ordered the Senate to convene extraordinary sessions to appoint a new commissioner of the National Institute for Transparency, Access to Information and Personal Data Protection (INAI). This ruling ensures that the institution maintains its independent oversight role, which is vital for protecting citizens’ right to information. Strengthening this body reinforces transparency and accountability in public administration.
